system:
You are a computational cancer biologist searching CRISPR screen data for selective genetic dependencies: genes that cancer cells with a particular alteration (the biomarker) need more than other cancer cells do. Such genes are candidate drug targets with a built-in patient-selection strategy.

Work like a careful scientist:
1. Plan first with write_plan, and revise it as you learn.
2. Survey the data (genome_wide_top, scan_biomarker, scan_target) to generate candidate hypotheses.
3. Be sceptical before you believe a signal. Use inspect_association to check whether it is driven by one lineage or a disease subtype hiding inside a lineage, and whether the effect is large enough to matter. Ask whether the biology makes sense (paralog buffering, pathway dependence, oncogene addiction). A broadly essential target may lack a therapeutic window.
4. Literature search is not available in this session: judge novelty and mechanism from the data and your reasoning.
5. Register only your best hypotheses (register_hypothesis). Registration is final and must come before replication. You have 5 replications, each of which must pass one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad cell lines and independent Sanger screens.
6. Report honestly with submit_findings. A hypothesis is replicated only if replicate() said so. Negative results are results. Never let what you remember from the literature override what the data show.

You have at most 15 model turns. Batch independent tool calls in one turn.
task_prompt:
Patient population of interest: cancers with biomarker MUT_G05367 (damaging mutation in gene G05367).

Find the single best candidate therapeutic target for this population: the gene these cell lines depend on most selectively, supported by the data. Register your top candidate (you may register up to two), replicate it, and submit findings with your best candidate listed first.

content.thinking: G00075 is the strongest candidate: it holds up across lineages, with 19 of 57 strongly dependent versus 12 of 569, so it's not broadly essential. I'll register it against MUT_G05367. The mechanism is still unclear since the gene IDs are anonymized, so I should be upfront that any explanation is inferred, most plausibly synthetic lethality with loss of G05367 or a related pathway member. I can't check novelty from here, since it shows as not found in the literature, though that may just reflect the anonymization. The next step is to register it and replicate.

input.mechanism: Damaging mutation in G05367 creates a synthetic-lethal dependency on G00075, plausibly via buffering/compensatory pathway function that becomes essential when G05367 is lost. Data: lineage-adjusted beta -0.30 (q=6e-15), 19/57 altered lines strongly dependent vs 12/569 others, effect consistent across uterus, ovary, bowel, breast; target expressed equally in altered and other lines, not broadly essential.

output: Registered H1: MUT_G05367 -> more dependent on G00075. Discovery evidence frozen: t=-9.27, n_altered=57. Replication budget left: 5. Replication passes only if one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad lines and Sanger screens.

findings.claim: Cancer lines with damaging MUT_G05367 are selectively more dependent on G00075 (lineage-adjusted beta -0.30 discovery; -0.29 held-out Broad; -0.17 independent Sanger, all one-sided p<0.01). 33% of altered lines are strongly dependent vs ~2% of others; effect holds across uterine, ovarian, colorectal and breast lineages and G00075 is not broadly essential.

input.summary: Best candidate target for MUT_G05367 cancers is G00075. Its dependency was the strongest lineage-adjusted selective signal (q≈6e-15), robust to leaving out individual lineages, and replicated in held-out Broad lines (p≈2e-12) and an independent Sanger screen (p≈1e-5), though the Sanger effect is weaker. Caveats: gene identities are anonymized, so the mechanism (likely buffering of G05367 loss) is inferred rather than established; 57 altered lines is a modest sample; the effect is concentrated in endometrial and ovarian lines. Other candidates (G00106, G08727) were weaker or lineage-confounded and were not registered. Confidence is moderate because the mechanism is untested and the Sanger replication is weaker.
